description: mailbox.rs lines 414 and 519: m.role.as_ref().map(|r| r.to_string()) == Some(role_str.to_owned()) allocates two String values (the .to_string() and the Some(role_str.to_owned())) for every mailbox in the account. Idiomatic: m.role.as_ref().map_or(false, |r| r.to_string() == role_str) avoids one allocation; or better, if MailboxRole implements PartialEq<str>, use m.role.as_deref().map(|r| r.as_str()) style. Occurs in both the create and update paths in handle_mailbox_set. On large accounts this runs O(mailboxes) per set operation. Clarity: the == Some(X) pattern on a mapped option is a code smell that obscures intent.
title: Role uniqueness check allocates two Strings per comparison in a hot loop
